text:
mike: FYI — saw a near-OOM and throttle cascade in EUW2 this morning during an ad-hoc backfill. 3 inference pods hit OOM-ish memory pressure, node-level throttles kicked, and some requests 5xx'd.

ana: timeline? which backfill? :eyes:

mike: backfill job bf-2026-0315-09 ran at 06:12 UTC. It was a large prefix pre-warm + KV repopulate for a customer migration. spike started ~06:15 and peaked 06:22.

kai: logs show KV cache warm churn + big init batches — looks like continuous batching + prewarm hit memory ladder.

devon: are these dedicated nodes or shared pool?

mike: shared EUW2 general-pool (prod + backfill). We allowed backfill as low-priority batch but it didn't respect burst cap.

olivia: quick metrics: GPU mem usage per pod went from 48% -> 96% within 4m. node free memory dropped to ~200MB before oom_kill throttling. I have Grafana links: https://grafana.redwood/euw2/d/kv-warm

ana: deploy bot? any automated fallback executed?

sre-bot: [automated] autoscaler scaled nodes + started reclaim policies at 06:25 UTC. Scale-up latency ~3m because of AZ quota checks.

kai: scale latency + burst quota = bad combo. We didn't have fallback to reserve a small warm pool for KV-heavy jobs.

mike: root causes I see: (1) batch backfill allowed to run on prod shared pool without strict mem throttle, (2) autoscaler AZ quota checks delayed node creation, (3) no per-job memory cap on backfill containers.

devon: + note: the runtime's prefix cache allocates in-GPU memory aggressively on first touch. Backfill accessed many long-lived prefixes simultaneously. That multiplied per-request KV allocation.

ana: any customer impact?

mike: ~1200 requests failed (5xx) across two services for ~8m. Impacted low-throughput user routes (priority low), but some fanout calls to higher-tier routes experienced added latency.

olivia: cost note: scale-up used burst GPUs from on-demand so cost for those 20m = ~$1.2k. If this repeats monthly that's ~14k/yr wasted.

kai: mitigation ideas:
- enforce mem_limit on batch/backfill containers (cgroup + device plugin)
- add admission controller that rejects large prewarm jobs on shared pools
- allow backfill to target dedicated reserved pool or schedule to off-peak with quota check

devon: also: tune runtime KV eviction policy for backfill workloads (evict large prefixes lazily during warm instead of all-at-once).

mike: immediate actions taken:
- killed bf-2026-0315-09 at 06:33 UTC (manual)
- bumped autoscaler aggressive mode to prefer AZ with free quota (temporary)
- added short-term admission rule: reject any backfill > 50GB KV touch on shared pool (implemented 07:10 UTC)

ana: timeline snippet for postdoc:```
06:12 start bf-2026-0315-09 (backfill)
06:15 mem spike observed
06:22 node throttling & 5xx increase
06:25 autoscaler triggered (scale-up delay ~3m)
06:33 manual kill of backfill
06:40 traffic normalized
07:10 admission rule enforced
```

olivia: Proposed long-term items:
- reserved backfill capacity (night windows) + discounts (saves cost and risk)
- per-tenant queueing + max-memory-per-job enforcement in scheduler
- autoscaler: pre-check AZ quotas ahead of spike (predictive)
- runtime: introduce per-prefix soft limits and staged KV prewarm that respects global mem budget

kai: I can own scheduler change (per-job mem limits) — ETA 2 weeks for design, 5 weeks for rollout with tests.

devon: I'll prototype staged KV prewarm in the runtime repo, should have POC in ~10 days.

mike: ops: olivia can you open a cost-ticket and link to this thread?

olivia: opened TICKET-6523: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/TICKET-6523 — added cost calc + timeline.

ana: action owners + rough due dates:
- kai: scheduler mem limits (design) - 2026-04-01
- devon: KV staged prewarm POC - 2026-03-25
- mike: admission rule -> make permanent & expand tests - 2026-03-20
- olivia: cost ticket + reserved capacity proposal - 2026-03-24

mike: follow-ups: add synthetic test that simulates 10x prefix warm concurrency and run in CI to catch regressions.

kai: will add perf test job to infra repo.

sre-bot: [reminder] Incident summary required for weekly incident review. Tagging #incident-reports.

devon: quick Q — should we mark this Severity 2? impact limited but production 5xx occurred.

ana: I think S2 is right: short duration, partial impact, operational root cause.

mike: agreed S2. I'll draft the summary and link to TICKET-6523.

olivia: noted — I'll add cost annex and include runbook changes.

mike: thanks all. closing notes: avoid running big KV prewarms on shared pools without scheduler caps. we'll reconvene after owners post status updates. :thumbsup:
